title: Stockroom: trusted dual-EDA component library
note: Owner outcomes are the product source of truth. The historical engineering checklist is retained below as unweighted implementation history and must never be presented as product readiness.
product_scope: Windows-only component-library management for both KiCad and Altium. A capability ships only when both EDA workflows are supported. KiCad-only project management is deferred and removed from the current frontend; its backend and Git history are preserved.

active_work.objective: Finish exact-MPN-to-assets acquisition with the smallest possible user workload: use verified direct sources and reviewed provider automation, retain every usable file, convert supported provider packages into native outputs, and require exact identity plus semantic and cross-EDA verification before attachment.
active_work.refresh_policy: Manually refreshed at meaningful checkpoints; this is not real-time telemetry.

workstreams.name: Automatic MPN-To-Assets Acquisition
workstreams.owner: Codex · acquisition planning and provider adapters
workstreams.evidence: The isolated UL Canary profile now proves two coherent provider paths for Texas Instruments TPD6E05U06RVZR. The retained SnapMagic pair remains available. A real saved 79,884-byte DigiKey Ultra Librarian script ZIP then ran through installed AD26 in 12.8 seconds and activated all five required KiCad/Altium assets in exactly one Git transaction. Active KiCad provider ultralibrarian manifest sha256:f84d8d3530caba1a0a011b0a51dda42630fb7dbba5e3d376b4121229db1d8b47 is the exact source of active Altium provider digikey-ultralibrarian manifest sha256:5886053375092ddbdeb3b74b7dcdbbbb0b02b61fde0f0dbc1929617690bc174a. Reopen, immutable evidence resolution, native SchLib/PcbLib entry readback, and installed cross-EDA verification all passed for 8 connected terminals, 6 no-connect package pads, and 14 physical pads.
workstreams.blocker: One successful provider canary does not prove arbitrary-MPN completion. The production Stockroom profile still contains only incomplete IC51-0484-806, and provider availability, verified-cache reuse, deterministic generation, and fallback performance remain unqualified at scale.
workstreams.next_action: Run one live DigiKey multi-author canary that retains both SnapMagic and Ultra Librarian through the same signed-in surface, then exercise several unrelated MPN and package classes through browser acquisition, conversion, fallback, attachment, reopen, and evidence verification.

workstreams.name: CAD Evidence Composition And Variants
workstreams.owner: Codex · immutable evidence and cross-EDA validation
workstreams.evidence: Committed role manifests and active CAD pointers preserve exact identity, provider, content digest, validation, and compatible source-manifest links. The live DigiKey/UL canary searched retained KiCad variants, rejected the incompatible active SnapMagic geometry, promoted the compatible UL bundle without deleting alternatives, bound the derived Altium manifest to that exact source, and projected both tools through one transaction and one commit. Mutation tests prove rollback after a post-KiCad Altium failure and preserve dirty exact targets.
workstreams.blocker: The component UI does not yet expose retained variants or a deliberate coherent pair switch. Per-tool activation remains unsuitable for switching an already-complete incompatible pair.
workstreams.next_action: Expose retained variants and add a user-facing coherent pair selector that invokes the same one-transaction compatibility boundary.

workstreams.name: DigiKey Ultra Librarian Conversion
workstreams.owner: Codex · DigiKey browser adapter and guarded Altium bridge
workstreams.evidence: A real isolated Camoufox run reused saved DigiKey credentials, selected the exact product/model page, and downloaded TPD6E05U06RVZR.zip. The 79,884-byte Altium choice is script based and contains STEP, one ASCII component payload, and the reviewed Ultra Librarian importer. The saved archive ran through installed AD26 in the normal guarded converter, produced one exact TPD6E05U06RVZR SchLib entry and one RVZ0014A PcbLib entry, selected a geometrically compatible retained UL KiCad set, preserved original and derived immutable evidence, and attached all five assets in one 12.8-second transaction. Independent installed readback proved 8 connected terminals, 6 no-connect mappings, and 14 matching pads. No X2 process or task-owned conversion/materialization directory remained. The duplicate WebView2 provider driver is retired. DigiKey now captures SnapMagic and Ultra Librarian as separate author routes under one session, binds every receipt to surface plus author, rejects mixed-route landed lists, ranks distributor-prefixed variants by CAD-author family, and retries a visible transient DigiKey export error with at most three fresh exact-route attempts. The real-DOM route regression and complete capture directory pass 321 tests.
workstreams.blocker: One part and package class do not prove arbitrary-MPN availability, account behavior, or throughput. The current acquisition timing starts from an already-downloaded archive, so browser navigation/download time is not included.
workstreams.next_action: Run a live DigiKey canary with both embedded author rows, then qualify unrelated MPNs and package classes through the full browser-to-archive path and measure provider gates, bounded retry recovery, and total wall time separately.

outcome_gates.name: Resilient Batch Automation
outcome_gates.measure: Automatic arbitrary-MPN asset completion is not yet proven. Verified-cache, permitted direct/open, deterministic-generation, and policy-permitted adapter foundations are incomplete; a managed user-driven commercial-page fallback is implemented in source but not deployed.
outcome_gates.acceptance: After one list import and one-time credential setup, Stockroom processes every unambiguous part through a resumable batch pipeline, retries transient failures, falls back across allowed providers or verified generators, and asks the user only about quarantined exceptions. Repeated decisions become reusable rules.
evidence: Owner direction: the current workflow is too slow and unmanageable.

Owner clarification 2026-07-28: clicking each provider download is too manual. The policy-compliant primary lane must therefore maximize verified-cache reuse, permitted direct/open retrieval, deterministic generation, and separately approved adapters. Commercial provider pages remain user-driven: Stockroom opens the page and owns interception, validation, attachment, and allowed fallback; the user owns login, exact-result and format selection, Download controls, CAPTCHA, and license acceptance.

The vNext provider runtime rejects ineligible or inexact providers, falls through classified failures automatically, binds saved plans to current policy and registration semantics before effects, and fails closed unless executable KiCad and Altium routes both exist. The proof uses synthetic adapters and does not yet replace the current capture path.

Workflow handlers now persist only sanitized policy, plan, receipt, and immutable evidence digests; rate limits become bounded durable retries, evidence fixed points become one compact decision, setup failures are classified, drift has zero adapter effects, and reopening WorkflowStore reuses the exact checkpoint. The combined provider suites pass 56 tests.

The Windows WorkflowCoordinator now polls the durable runtime with bounded fair workers, reopens expired claims, rejects stale service generations, stops cleanly, and exposes only sanitized counters; four focused real-Windows tests pass.

Configured Mouser and DigiKey metadata clients now run through an exact-identity adapter and atomic local evidence CAS. The runtime rejects forged, missing, mismatched, or tampered evidence, and its configured production composition cannot omit the verifier. The authenticated coordinator endpoint exposes counters only and returns 503 until a persistent owner is mounted.

Commit 3a296a1e reports exact provider model absence instead of inventing a file. Commit caf031a7 adds a Stockroom-managed, exact-provider-page download fallback that intercepts files through the task broker without reading credentials or driving controls; production runner/API wiring remains uncommitted and the installed app remains on 3a296a1e. The working-tree HUD shows exact identity, required formats, live receipt count, and explicit Finish/Try Another Provider/Cancel actions; nine focused tests pass. The policy audit found that Ultra Librarian prohibits robot access, so its commercial page remains user-driven. Ultra Librarian's official 2025-10-16 announcement now establishes a native Altium bundle with schematic library, PCB library, LibPkg, and integrated STEP. outcome_gates.name: One-To-Thousand Responsive UX
outcome_gates.measure: Synthetic durable backend correctness passes at 100 and 1,000 identities; 1,000 items now settle in 28.838 seconds against a 30-second scheduler budget
outcome_gates.acceptance: The same workflow handles one or 1,000 parts. Submission acknowledges immediately; completed results stream incrementally; search, filtering, review, pause, resume, retry, and cancel stay responsive; restarting never repeats successful expensive work.
evidence: Owner direction: the workflow must feel easy, intuitive, and responsive at both one part and 1,000 parts.

A fault-injected synthetic harness settles both 100 and 1,000 exact identities through the same persisted 14-stage graph, including a mid-run reopen, zero human decisions, and exactly-once terminal receipts. The 100-item Windows baseline is 3.290 seconds at 427.37 dispatches/second.

The initial exact 1,000-item run completed correctly but took 65.530 seconds. SQL profiling isolated same-process BEGIN IMMEDIATE contention and duplicate persisted-graph traversal; a process-local writer gate and indexed, single-pass graph verification reduced the exact rerun to 28.838 seconds at 487.52 dispatches/second.

The optimized run retained all 14,059 dispatches, 1,000 publications and receipts, 49,187 events, one mid-run reopen, terminal_exactly_once=true, WAL/FULL production-store semantics, and the four durable publication checkpoints. The workflow suite passes 73 tests.
The harness explicitly simulates provider, Git, catalog, and asset effects. Its correctness result is not evidence for production completion or UI responsiveness.
blockers: Qualify the 30-second scheduler budget across supported Windows hardware while production provider and EDA effects are introduced; the current measured margin is 1.16 seconds.
Virtualize large UI collections and stream durable stage/result events instead of polling whole aggregates.
Set latency and memory budgets from the first measured Windows baseline, then enforce them in gates.

items.name: Derive Engine
items.why: The owner's acceptance test lives here: change the naming scheme, re-derive, lose nothing.

steps.t: Recompute the whole derived block from sourced/
steps.evidence: app/backend/stockroom/derive/engine.py: derive_block(identity, payloads) -> Derived, reading only sourced/ via model.sourced.read_json. Reuse-by-extraction: parse_mouser_payload/parse_digikey_payload were pulled OUT of the credentialed adapters (lookup() now calls them), so a re-derive runs with NO API keys on a fresh clone - which device parity requires. 25 tests in tests/backend/derive.

steps.t: IDEMPOTENT: derive twice, byte-identical records
steps.evidence: test_deriving_twice_gives_a_byte_identical_record compares the SERIALIZED record (json.dumps sort_keys), not the dataclass, because a git diff would show an ordering difference an object compare misses. Plus test_the_derivation_does_not_depend_on_a_clock: derived_at is a PARAMETER, and 2020 vs 2099 changes that field and NOTHING else. Plus test_the_merge_follows_REGISTRY_priority: determinism is what idempotency rests on. MUTATION-PROVEN: time.time() in derived_by -> 4 failed; merging in payload order -> 1 failed.

steps.t: LOSSLESS: a derive never writes under sourced/
steps.evidence: Measured TWO independent ways. (1) EFFECT: test_a_derive_never_writes_under_sourced sha256-hashes every file under sourced/ before and after THREE derives, and refuses to pass if nothing was seeded. (2) MECHANISM: assert_no_writer_imported walks the AST of every derive module for a call to write_*/unlink/rmtree/rename - an AST, not a substring search, because 'write_payload' appears in the docstrings and a string test would have to exempt the very file most likely to break the rule. MUTATION-PROVEN: adding a write_payload call -> 4 failed.

steps.t: Naming scheme swappable by config, not by editing code
steps.evidence: derive/naming.py: SCHEMES registry ('spec-aware','mpn','manufacturer-mpn') selected by NAME; get_scheme raises UnknownNamingScheme rather than silently defaulting. test_changing_the_naming_scheme_renames_without_touching_anything_else asserts all three names differ, that EVERY other derived field is byte-identical across them, and that sourced/ hashes are unchanged. REJECTED a format-string template and a config-file category table, both recorded in the module docstring with why. MUTATION-PROVEN: a silent fallback on a typo -> 1 failed.

steps.t: Normalization executes at derive time with raw sourced evidence preserved
steps.evidence: Normalization now RUNS at derive time and is mutation-proven (removing normalize_specs from derive_block fails a test that asserts on the engine's own return value, not through the record - which was itself a fix, since PartRecord.derived normalizes in both its getter and setter and masked the engine entirely). The IMPORT PATH still normalizes too, and that is now HARMLESS rather than lossy: every one of the 158 records carries its raw vendor payloads under sourced/, so the pre-normalization answer survives and is re-derivable. PROVEN END TO END: a derivation bug (canonical fields being dropped) was fixed by re-deriving all 158 records from stored evidence in 0.4s with ZERO API calls, where before the split it would have needed a full ~25min quota-paced re-import. Lifecycle went from absent-on-all-158 to present-on-158.

steps.t: Merged to main, gate green
steps.evidence: Committed 1978e3f on main. Full backend suite 3460 passed / 5 skipped / exit 0 (2m30s, -n 12); ruff clean on the new package. The 460 pre-existing enrich tests still pass after extracting the pure payload parsers out of the two credentialed adapters (reuse-by-extraction, not a copy).

items.name: Requirements By Part Class
items.why: Fixes 136 requirements nothing could ever satisfy: passives were being asked for Altium symbol and footprint.

steps.t: requirements = f(part_class, tool) off the EDA registry
steps.evidence: RECONCILED 2026-07-27, not rebuilt: capture/requirements.py::capture_needs already IS f(part_class, tool) off the registry - it walks `_capturable()` (every tool's registered capturable_assets) and intersects with `record.capturable(tool_key)` (the part class's kinds). No `if tool ==` and no `if passive` anywhere in the path. The step was left unticked when its siblings shipped.

steps.t: passive resolves to [] for EVERY tool
steps.evidence: model/part_class.py CLASS_NEEDS + needed_kinds()/capturable_kinds() intersect the class's asset kinds with the EDA registry's closable_assets()/capturable_assets(). No 'if tool ==' and no 'if passive' anywhere in the path. tests/backend/model/test_part_class.py, 16 tests.

steps.t: mechanical = footprint only, virtual = nothing and no BOM line
steps.evidence: DRIVEN for real over all four classes x both registered tools: passive -> [], virtual -> []. NEGATIVE CONTROL: component -> ['kicad_symbol','kicad_footprint','kicad_model','altium_symbol','altium_footprint'], so the empty results are not an instrument that always returns empty. Before this rule the surface demanded altium_symbol+altium_footprint from all 68 of the owner's passives: 136 unsatisfiable requirements.

steps.t: requires_override wins over the class default
steps.evidence: DRIVEN: mechanical -> ['kicad_footprint','altium_footprint'] (footprint only, never a symbol); virtual -> [] with has_bom_line=False, while every other class is True. tests test_a_mechanical_part_needs_a_footprint_and_no_symbol / test_a_virtual_part_needs_nothing_and_has_no_bom_line.

steps.t: Requirement enum still matches the TypeScript union
steps.evidence: test_an_override_replaces_the_class_default, test_an_override_that_needs_NOTHING_is_different_from_no_override_at_all (null vs needs=[] are distinct claims), test_an_override_can_be_scoped_to_one_tool, plus round-trip and forward-compat-key tests. Mirrored in the frontend: 2 new edaTarget tests, mutation-proven.

steps.t: Merged to main, gate green
steps.evidence: GAP FOUND AND CLOSED. The match was asserted in a COMMENT in capture/requirements.py and enforced by NOTHING. Added test_the_requirement_enum_matches_the_typescript_union_exactly + the same for PartClass, parsing the TS string unions out of types.ts. TAMPERED 3 ways, all caught: dropped a TS member; added a TS-only PartClass ('panel'); added a Python-only member (EAGLE_SYMBOL). Restored green.

items.name: Index Schema
items.why: Today the index physically cannot express 'has an Altium footprint'. It is single-tool, single-asset, and rebuilt from scratch every sync.

steps.t: Per-tool columns by iterating the EDA registry
steps.evidence: part_assets CHILD TABLE, one row per (part, tool, kind), populated by iterating all_tools() x ASSET_KINDS. REJECTED wide per-tool columns: they fix today's case and keep the real problem, since a THIRD tool would need a schema migration. New queries the old shape could not answer AT ALL: assets_for_tool(tool), parts_missing_asset(tool, kind) - the latter a LEFT JOIN so a part with no row for that tool counts as missing it rather than being silently excluded (mutation-proven: an INNER JOIN fails 2 tests).

steps.t: Multiple purchase rows, not one purchase_url
steps.evidence: part_purchase child table, one row per link with vendor/url/part_number/stock/currency, seq preserving the record's priority order. The old single purchase_url column kept only purchase[0], so every other distributor's link and order number was invisible to every query. New: purchase_rows(part_id), vendors(). Mutation-proven: indexing only purchase[0] again fails a test.

steps.t: Incremental sync, no DROP TABLE
steps.evidence: No DROP TABLE anywhere in _SCHEMA (asserted by a test), every object IF NOT EXISTS, and sync() upserts by comparing a sha256 of each record file's BYTES against a stored source_hash. CONTENT, not mtime: a 'touch' must not count as a change, and this repo has already shipped a bug from treating an mtime as one. Both directions tested - a touched but unchanged file parses 0 records, and an edit that keeps the same length still parses 1 (which a size-or-mtime check would miss). Removal is explicit: a record file that disappears has its parts row AND its child rows deleted, which the old full-rebuild got for free by dropping everything and an incremental path has to do on purpose. ctx.rebuild_index() now calls sync() instead of close+rebuild. 4 mutations run, all caught.

steps.t: Measured before/after on a synthetic 10k library
steps.evidence: MEASURED on a synthetic 10,000-record library. Cold build (parse all 10k) 0.50s. sync with nothing changed: 0.14s, 10000 unchanged / 0 PARSED. sync after ONE edit: 0.14s, 9999 unchanged / 1 parsed. So a library write went from re-parsing 10k records to parsing 1 - a 3.7x wall-clock win, NOT the 100x the parse saving alone suggests, because the residual 0.14s is reading and hashing all 10k files and I am not claiming otherwise. Also measured: search 29ms, facets 1.9ms, parts_missing_asset(altium,footprint) 5.4ms over 10k - the last being a query that was impossible before.

steps.t: Expresses TRUST, not just presence
steps.evidence: part_assets stores origin_vendor/origin_url/origin_captured_at and checks_json - the raw CHECK FACTS. NO VERDICT COLUMN EXISTS (asserted by a test reading PRAGMA table_info). asset_trust() derives PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN through model.trust.verdict_for on every read, so tightening a check re-judges the library with no re-audit. UNKNOWN for an unmeasured asset, never a pass. assets_by_origin() counts unattributed assets under '(unrecorded)' rather than dropping them, because 'we do not know where this came from' is the answer the owner's complaint ('its not trusted where we've gotten them') most needs. Mutation-proven: returning a fixed verdict fails 2 tests.

steps.t: Search, facets and parametric filters still green
steps.evidence: 693 store + api tests pass unchanged (search, facets, duplicates, parametric filters, completion rollup), plus an explicit test that the public read API - count/search/facets/find_by_mpn/get - behaves identically. The schema changed underneath; the contract did not.

steps.t: Merged to main, gate green
steps.evidence: Implemented on current main by commit 60044f2f (the formerly recorded 05b3ac9 does not exist). Full backend suite at the time: 3550 passed / 5 skipped / exit 0; ruff clean. 16 new index tests, 6 mutations all caught. Historical UI evidence used the former 158-part library, which has since been intentionally cleared.

waves.name: Build (2 parallel)
waves.why: Both read the derive engine, so they wait for wave 1 to land.

items.name: Importer
items.why: The library is being deleted and rebuilt, so this is the tool that does it. No migration needed.

steps.t: Takes the MPN register, pulls Mouser + DigiKey
steps.evidence: scripts/import_library.py + importer/engine.py. DRIVEN LIVE against the owner's real Mouser + DigiKey keys (read from the Windows install's config.json via --config): both APIs answered for TPS62130RGTR and both payloads were stored. Worklist is the library's own records, deterministic id order.

steps.t: Writes sourced/<id>/<vendor>.json verbatim
steps.evidence: VERBATIM, measured: the test compares the stored payload for equality AND for KEY ORDER, which a sorted re-serialization would silently break (json.dumps(json.loads(x)) loses order, and that is how the old schema already lost a value). Live proof: sourced/tps62130rgtr-d77f/{mouser,digikey}.json, 2 files / 24470 bytes.

steps.t: Calls the existing derive engine, does not write a second one
steps.evidence: importer/engine.py imports rederive from stockroom.derive.engine and contains NO derivation logic. test_the_import_re_derives_by_CALLING_the_derive_engine. Live result: 38 specs, display_name 'Switching Voltage Regulator 16-VQFN', category ICs, value TPS62130RGTR - all produced by the derive engine from the stored evidence.

steps.t: Classifies each part into one of the four classes
steps.evidence: importer/classify.py: four classes as a keyword TABLE behind an electrical veto, defaulting to COMPONENT. MEASURED over the owner's real 158 records: 85 passive / 72 component / 1 mechanical (the M3 screw 29311 - exactly the part the spec says was excluded by hand). NEGATIVE CONTROL run on 8 cases including 3 adversarial ones (a heatsink-mounted regulator, a SCREW terminal connector, a RESISTOR network driver) - all correctly stay COMPONENT. Found 17 genuinely-passive parts currently stored as component because the v2->v3 migration defaulted them; each verified by eye as R/C/L.

steps.t: Rate-limited part is DEFERRED, not FAILED
steps.evidence: Outcome enum separates DEFERRED (a provider refused for quota/rate reasons - retryable, part left UNCHANGED, no evidence written) from NO_DATA (every source answered and none knows the MPN) and FAILED. Decided by the provider's own last_status against DEFERRABLE_STATUSES, never guessed from a missing body. Both directions tested, including the negative control that a not_found is NOT deferred.

steps.t: Stoppable and resumable, worklist derived from library state
steps.evidence: No checkpoint file by design: needs_sources() asks the tree whether sourced/<id>/<source>.json exists, so Ctrl-C and re-run continues where it stopped. Proven by API-CALL COUNT, not by file state: a second pass returns SKIPPED and the fake fetcher records zero calls, i.e. it does not re-spend quota. --refetch is the deliberate opposite.

steps.t: Merged to main, gate green
steps.evidence: Committed 0e4ae8c. Full backend suite 3499 passed / 5 skipped / exit 0 (2m09s, -n 12); ruff clean. 35 importer tests + a guard that makes urlopen explode, added after MEASURING that my own first pacing test made a real outbound request to api.mouser.com with a bogus key.

items.name: Automatic Acquisition And Guided Fallback
items.why: The primary path must turn one or 1,000 MPNs into validated assets automatically. Guided interaction is reserved for genuine provider gates because every unnecessary click is multiplied by the batch size.

steps.t: Every vendor shown by guided capture has a matching executable adapter
steps.evidence: INVALIDATED by the 2026-07-27 composition audit and the later provider-policy audit. Discovery advertises DigiKey, Ultra Librarian, SamacSys, and SnapMagic, but only some have code paths, unsupported selections silently execute Ultra Librarian, and Ultra Librarian prohibits robot access. URL discovery or DOM-driving code is not an approved executable provider capability.

steps.t: Catch, classify and attach the downloaded file
steps.evidence: attach_assets takes an origin and applies it to symbol, footprint AND 3D -- the path guided capture actually uses, not just attach_symbol/attach_footprint. Route accepts {vendor,url}; server stamps the time. capture.tsx sends the vendor picked in VendorPicker. TAMPER-PROVEN both ends: dropping the origin in the frontend fails a test, making the pipeline never record one fails another. 54ae1b2.

steps.t: Record origin {vendor, url, captured_at} on the asset
steps.evidence: `model/asset.py::AssetOrigin` was built for the owner's complaint ("its not trusted where we've gotten them") and NOTHING populated it - every attach produced origin: None. Now: attach_symbol/attach_footprint take an origin, `POST /parts/{id}/symbol|footprint` accept {vendor,url}, and `LibraryIndex.assets_by_vendor()` makes 'where did these come from' a QUERY. captured_at is stamped by the SERVER, never accepted from the caller - a timestamp a client can set is not evidence. Repointing a reference DROPS the old origin rather than leaving one vendor's name on another's file, and an attach naming no vendor stays honestly unattributed (None, not ""). 9 tests; TAMPER-PROVEN twice (trusting the caller's timestamp fails 3, keeping a stale origin across a repoint fails 1). STILL OPEN: the guided KiCad path commits through ingest `attach_assets`, a different seam that does not yet carry the origin - logged in the Punch List.

steps.t: Both formats per part where the vendor offers them
steps.evidence: ONE REAL PART PROVED, ARBITRARY MPN STILL OPEN. The saved DigiKey/UL TPD6E05U06RVZR package ran through installed AD26 and activated KiCad symbol, footprint, STEP plus native Altium SchLib/PcbLib in one transaction. Reopen and installed cross-EDA readback passed. Direct Ultra Librarian's current native-export route and unrelated MPN/package availability remain unqualified: https://www.ultralibrarian.com/native_export_for_altium_designer.

steps.t: Fast path to the next part
steps.evidence: REBUILT IN THE WORKING TREE, NOT YET SHIPPED. The Stockroom-owned provider HUD has explicit Finish, Try Another Provider, and Cancel actions; Try Another ends only the current provider attempt so the ranked fallback can continue. The HUD also shows the exact identity, required formats, and live captured-file count. Focused lifecycle tests pass, but no installed-page screenshot or live provider run exists.

steps.t: Designed deliberately, screenshot critiqued both themes
steps.evidence: The working-tree HUD has deliberate compact, keyboard-movable, collapsible, forced-colors, reduced-motion, and live-status behavior behind a closed shadow root. Its injection and action contract are tested, but it has not been rendered or visually audited on a real provider page in either native Windows theme.

steps.t: Merged to main, gates green incl. frontend-dist
Verified cache, permitted direct/open retrieval, and deterministic generation run before any commercial browser lane
steps.evidence: The task-bound acquisition broker and exact-identity validation seams exist, but no arbitrary-MPN production run proves a verified-cache, permitted-direct/open, and evidence-driven-generation policy through complete KiCad, native Altium, and STEP attachment.

steps.t: Only separately policy-approved adapters automate; commercial provider pages remain user driven
steps.evidence: Existing provider planning proves capability-ranked fallback mechanics, but automatic execution requires a separately reviewed machine-access contract. Ultra Librarian prohibits robot access. On commercial pages Stockroom may open the exact page and capture downloads, but the user must perform login, result and format selection, Download controls, CAPTCHA, and license acceptance.

steps.t: User-driven exact-provider capture exists as a fallback, not the primary bulk workflow
steps.evidence: Commit caf031a7 adds exact-page managed-Chromium interception, task-bound saved bytes, explicit finish/page-close/cancel/timeout completion, and no credential or DOM driving. The working tree adds an exact-identity HUD with required formats, live receipt count, Finish, Try Another Provider, and Cancel. Stockroom owns opening, interception, validation, attachment, and allowed fallback; the user owns every provider-side interaction. One-part/one-provider production wiring and the HUD are not deployed.

steps.t: Capture browser avoids the Windows firewall prompt
steps.evidence: Commit 15db4098 removes RTCPeerConnection and webkitRTCPeerConnection before page code runs and has focused initialization tests. The installed checkout predates the commit, so installed interactive proof remains open.

steps.t: Exact validated artifacts can compose across providers without weakening verification
steps.evidence: LIVE AND MUTATION VERIFIED. Partial role manifests bind exact identity, provider, adapter, role, bytes, validation report, and source manifests. The real DigiKey/UL Altium delivery rejected incompatible active SnapMagic geometry, selected and promoted one compatible retained UL KiCad bundle, and bound both active pointers in one transaction. The five installed assets reopened and passed native and cross-EDA readback. Failure injection proves zero-trace rollback.

steps.t: Every exact validated variant is preserved and active selection is explicit
steps.evidence: PARTIAL. The working-tree role index is append-only and retains role, source, digest, validation, and compatibility source-manifest links for every exact validated variant. Ultra Librarian ranks before SnapMagic by default, but ranking does not mutate active references. The explicit reversible active-set selector and UI are still pending.

steps.t: Installed end-to-end arbitrary-MPN proof attaches validated KiCad, native Altium, and STEP outputs
steps.evidence: ONE ISOLATED CANARY PASSED, ARBITRARY MPN AND INSTALLED-UI PROOF REMAIN OPEN. TPD6E05U06RVZR passed saved archive, installed AD26 conversion, exact identity, semantic readback, cross-EDA equivalence, one-transaction attachment, reopen, active source binding, and evidence-digest resolution. Browser acquisition time and unrelated MPN/package classes are not yet qualified.

waves.name: Prove It
waves.why: Nothing ships to the real library until these pass. A failed acceptance test reported honestly beats a green claim.

items.name: Cold-Eyes Review, Verified And Fixed
items.why: One fresh subagent reviewed the diff (07db6a8..6d27dba) with no plan or reasoning context, per the owner's standing rule. It found 11 real defects, most with a mutation proving they were real and a negative control proving the check wasn't vacuous. All 11 fixed same session, each re-verified with the SAME mutation.

steps.t: Finding 1 (CRITICAL): fetch_payload used HTTP-truthiness ('ok' if body else 'not_found') to decide a hit, but a genuine not-found is HTTP 200 with an EMPTY results list - a truthy dict. A fabricated MPN was indistinguishable from a real hit: written to sourced/, indexed, counted imported, and never retried.
steps.evidence: mouser.py + digikey_api.py fetch_payload now parse the body the same way lookup() already did correctly. Re-ran the reviewer's exact negative control: real hit -> ok/not-None, ZZZNOTAREALPART123 -> not_found/None, on BOTH adapters. 4 new regression tests in tests/backend/enrich/{test_mouser,test_digikey_api}.py.

steps.t: Finding 2: the writer-check's own 'can it fail' test built a synthetic AST from a string and asserted ast.walk() finds a call in it - testing the ast module, not the gate. MEASURED to be vacuous: disabling the real gate left it green.
steps.evidence: Split engine.assert_no_writer_imported into _scan_modules_for_writes(modules, writer), callable directly. Rewrote the self-test to drive it against an injected temp module with a real write_payload() call PLUS a negative control (a clean module must not raise). Reproduced the reviewer's exact mutation (disable the gate) -> now correctly FAILS; restored -> green.

steps.t: Finding 3 (CRITICAL): the DetailPanel's own 'Add X to make this part usable' line hardcoded symbol/footprint/3D-model regardless of part_class, recreating the exact class-blindness bug edaTarget.ts fixed - one layer up, in the same session.
steps.evidence: missingAssets now derives from kicad.missing (already class-aware); hasModel's stock-3D inheritance narrowed from 'any class needing no owned model' to 'passive specifically' (a mechanical footprint is not guaranteed to carry a baked-in 3D body the way a KiCad stock passive footprint is). Drove the reviewer's exact 4-row reproduction table against the REAL RENDERED DOM: all 4 passed after the fix, 3 of 4 FAILED against the pre-fix code (mutation-proven). 4 permanent tests added to DetailPanel.test.tsx; first version of those tests was itself vacuous (canComplete gate never enabled) and caught before being trusted.

steps.t: Finding 4: an exception anywhere in one part's import could kill the WHOLE pass. UnknownNamingScheme subclasses Exception not ValueError so it escaped the catch tuple; a per-source fetch was not wrapped in any try at all.
steps.evidence: Fetch loop now catches Exception per-source (result.errors); the write/derive/reclassify catch widened from a hand-picked tuple to Exception (BaseException still uncaught). 2 regression tests: a raising fetcher across 3 parts still produces a report covering all 3; a bad --scheme fails only that part, never the batch.

steps.t: Finding 5: a payload written then a failure BEFORE the record was persisted left orphaned evidence that resumability (file-existence-based, by design) would never retry - permanently, silently, in the skipped bucket forever.
steps.evidence: import_part now detects files present but absent from record.sources ('orphaned'), indexes them WITHOUT re-fetching, and re-derives. 2 regression tests: recovery happens with a fetcher that raises if called at all (proves no re-fetch); a second pass after recovery is a clean SKIPPED.

steps.t: Finding 6: sources.py's docstring claimed a drift gate (tests/backend/importer/test_source_registry.py) that did not exist.
steps.evidence: Wrote the real file: fetch/parse registries must name the same sources, in the same relative priority order, plus a self-test that the drift logic can fail (feeds it a deliberately broken pair).

steps.t: Finding 7: load_payloads swallowed an invalid-v3-id ValueError as 'no evidence', so rederive() (a public entry point) could silently BLANK a record's derived block instead of refusing loudly.
steps.evidence: load_payloads now raises loudly for an invalid id; import_part's own id check moved to the top of the function, UNCONDITIONAL on --refetch (previously only checked in the non-refetch branch, so --refetch on a bad id would have spent real API quota before failing).

steps.t: Finding 8: pace() iterated a set (nondeterministic order) and ran for every record regardless of whether it needed a fetch - throttling a resumed pass for work it was never going to do.
steps.evidence: usable is now sorted(); pacing gated on _needs_a_fetch() per record. Regression test: a fully-imported part triggers zero pace() calls; a fresh part still triggers one (negative control).

steps.t: Finding 9: the electrical veto's whole-word matching had NO trailing \b on all but the last alternative, so 'led' matched inside 'ledge' and 'gate' inside 'Gateway' - the exact substring-matching failure the module's own thesis warns against.
steps.evidence: Every alternative now closes with its own \b. Verified: 'Aluminium ledge bracket' and 'Gateway enclosure' now correctly match their sibling controls ('Steel bracket', 'Enclosure') instead of being wrongly excused to component.

steps.t: Finding 10: the writer-check's FORBIDDEN_CALLS included bare 'replace'/'rename' attribute names, which collide with str.replace/Path.replace - a latent false-positive machine waiting for the first text.replace() in the derive path.
steps.evidence: Narrowed to {unlink, rmtree} only, neither a name any object in this path's real vocabulary (str, dict, dataclass) exposes.

steps.t: Finding 11: dead `import sys` in derive/engine.py (invisible to ruff, F401 is globally ignored by design), and a comment pointing at lib/partFields.ts, which was never created.
steps.evidence: import removed; comment corrected to state reality (detail.derived.<field>, no dedicated helper module exists).

steps.t: Categories the review checked and found CLEAN: no existing test was weakened (assertion/case counts equal or higher in every rewritten file, exactly 3 expect() lines strengthened not deleted); no blanket find/replace damage to dev-ids/comments/string literals; no consumer reads a field that no longer exists at runtime.
steps.evidence: Reported by the reviewer with counts per file; independently re-verified via full suites (backend 3513 passed/5 skipped, frontend 1260 passed, tsc clean, build clean, ruff clean) after all 11 fixes landed.

items.name: Migrate The Library To v3 Part Ids
items.why: BLOCKS THE IMPORT OF THE REAL LIBRARY, found 2026-07-27 by pointing the importer at it. 84 of 158 records still carry pre-v3 ids with underscores (`103at_2`), and `sourced/` correctly refuses those as path components - so evidence cannot be filed for any of them. The other 74 are path-safe but still lack the `-hash` suffix. The importer now reports this as one FAILED part with the reason instead of crashing the pass.

steps.t: Rename every record to slug(mpn)+'-'+sha256(mpn)[:4], in one atomic commit
steps.evidence: app/backend/stockroom/migrate/v3_ids.py + scripts/migrate_library_v3.py, APPLIED to the real 158-part library (commit 2966668). git detected 198 RENAMES rather than 158 deletes+adds, so file history is preserved. Verified independently of the tool's own report: 158 records in / 158 out, 158 distinct MPNs (no merges), schema_version 3 on all 158, 0 v2 keys left, all 158 carry derived + part_class.

steps.t: Rewrite every reference to a renamed id (index, projects, assign bindings)
steps.evidence: Every persisted reference enumerated by READING the library, not assuming. MOVED: parts/<id>.json (158) and datasheets/<id>.pdf (85 of 158 - measured: all 85 named exactly <id>.pdf, zero other conventions) with record.datasheet.file updated in the same pass -> 0 dangling datasheet refs after. NOT TOUCHED, each checked: models/ (named by MPN, zero refs embed an id), symbols/ + footprints/ (per-CATEGORY libs), the SQLite index (derived, rebuilt), altium/*.DbLib (regenerated + gitignored). REPORTED not migrated: project _sr_bound_part_id bindings live in the PROJECT's repo - measured zero registered projects on either of the owner's libraries, and the tool REFUSES unless --allow-orphan-bindings when any exist.

steps.t: Prove no two records collide onto one id, and no id is left path-unsafe
steps.evidence: Collision detection refuses rather than merging: two records mapping to one id would DESTROY one, so it is a blocking error naming both. Also refuses a filename that disagrees with the record's id (picking a winner is not a migration's call) and a record with no MPN (the id is slug(mpn)+sha256(mpn)[:4], so there is nothing to compute). Verified on the real library: 0 collisions, 0 path-UNSAFE ids afterwards (was 84 of 158), 0 filename/id disagreements. 17 tests; 5 mutations run, all caught - dropping collision detection, unlinking before writing, forgetting the datasheet ref, forgetting the id update, accepting a filename mismatch.

steps.t: Dry run first, and a verified backup before it is applied
steps.evidence: DRY RUN IS THE DEFAULT; --apply is required. Backup is git itself: the library is a git repo, so a clean tree + recorded HEAD is a complete verified undo (git checkout . && git clean -fd, printed on success). REFUSES to apply against a DIRTY library tree because git is then no longer a full undo - and that check is SCOPED to the library path, after finding that a bare git status reported the whole repo's churn and would have made --allow-dirty the normal way to run it. Ran dry first against the real library (158 planned, 0 errors), then --apply from HEAD d852ecb2 clean.

items.name: Acceptance Test
items.why: The owner's own bar, verbatim: 'we can edit it without reimporting'.

steps.t: Import real parts into a scratch library
steps.evidence: Real parts into a scratch library with real API calls: scripts/import_library.py --library <scratch> --config <windows config> --apply pulled Mouser AND DigiKey for TPS62130RGTR and wrote both payloads. Dry run verified FIRST by listing files afterwards (exactly the one seeded record, nothing else).

steps.t: Derive twice, prove byte-identical
steps.evidence: RE-PROVEN AT FULL SCALE on the real library via scripts/verify_derive.py: all 158 records, derive twice -> byte-identical record, PASS.

steps.t: Prove sourced/ untouched by either derive
steps.evidence: RE-PROVEN AT FULL SCALE: sourced/ tree sha256-hashed before and after 790 derives across 158 records (315 files, 5,464,197 bytes) - unchanged. PASS.

steps.t: Change the naming scheme, re-derive, identity survives
steps.evidence: RE-PROVEN AT FULL SCALE: every record re-derived under all three naming schemes; identity (id/mpn/manufacturer/part_class) survived every one, and a scheme swap changed ONLY display_name and nothing else in the derived block. PASS on 158/158.

items.name: Adversarial Review
items.why: This project has shipped a check that could not fail and an audit that was 100% false positives. Refute, do not confirm.

steps.t: Every new detector fed a known-BAD input
No presence-measuring code that reads like trust
No 'if tool ==' branch in shared logic
No success message emitted before the thing was observed
Nothing lost in the merges

items.name: Delete And Re-Import The Library
items.why: Step 2 of the owner's build order. Only after the schema is proven.

steps.t: Full backup of the current library taken and verified
steps.evidence: The library is a git repository, so the backup IS git and it is VERIFIED by content, not asserted: the pre-migration state is commit d852ecb2 and the pre-import state is 2966668, both pushed to origin. Recovering any record is 'git show <sha>:libraries/Stockroom/parts/<id>.json'. Verified the guard works: scripts/migrate_library_v3.py REFUSES to apply against a dirty library tree precisely because git is then no longer a complete undo, and that check is scoped to the library path (a bare git status reported the whole repo's churn and would have made --allow-dirty routine). No separate copy was taken deliberately - a second copy is a second thing to keep in sync, and git already holds every prior state.

items.name: Ruthless Critique Of The Real Windows Shots
items.why: Element-by-element pass over the 2026-07-27 real-Windows shots (dark Components, light Settings) at HEAD, per the standing screenshot directive. Split into DEFECTS (unambiguous, fix them) and DESIGN TENSIONS (need the owner to choose, because unilaterally re-laying-out a surface is what produced 'AHH the new ui sucks it moved everything').

steps.t: DEFECT, MEASURED: hover and selected are indistinguishable in LIGHT theme only. styles/index.css - dark: --c-acc-soft rgba(255,255,255,0.11) vs --c-hover rgba(255,255,255,0.03), ratio 0.27 (clearly distinct). light: --c-acc-soft rgba(0,0,0,0.06) vs --c-hover rgba(0,0,0,0.04), ratio 0.67 (nearly identical). So light theme diverges from the ratio the WORKING theme already proves. RECOMMENDED FIX, needs owner approval because --c-acc-soft has 30 uses across 12+ files and this repaints every selected state in light theme: raise light --c-acc-soft to 0.11 to match dark, giving ratio 0.36 and making the selected state the louder of the two (the correct direction). NOT applied unilaterally. CONFIRMED BY RE-SHOOT: on a shot with nothing hovered, ONLY the selected item carries a fill - so the second 'active-looking' item in the Windows shot was hover, exactly as the 0.67 ratio predicts.
DEFECT: the same state is spelled two ways on ONE screen - 'Up to Date!' (bottom-left, exclamation) vs 'Up To Date' (right). Design contract says Title Case for interactive labels
steps.evidence: FIXED: Rail.tsx 'Up to Date!' -> 'Up To Date', so the rail button and the Settings summary now spell the state identically and both obey the Title-Case-for-controls contract. Pure copy, zero layout change.

projects.name: Device Parity

waves.name: Updates That Cannot Be Blocked
waves.why: An update must never fail because of a file this machine created.

items.name: Untracked Files Blocking A Pull
items.why: The owner's laptop aborted every update on 10 SR-*.kicad_sym it had created locally.

steps.t: A pull clears untracked files an incoming commit would add
steps.evidence: GitRepo._clear_untracked_blockers: fetches, then moves aside only the paths the incoming commits ADD (--diff-filter=A) that are untracked locally. Reproduces the owners exact abort in a two-clone fixture and fixes it.

steps.t: A local file that DIFFERS is kept, never overwritten
steps.evidence: A local file whose git hash differs from the incoming blob is MOVED to .stockroom-kept keeping its path, never deleted. TAMPER-PROVEN: replacing the move with an unlink fails the test.

steps.t: An untracked file the update does not touch is left alone
steps.evidence: NARROWNESS. Only ADDED paths are touched; a bystander untracked file is untouched and no rescue dir is created. Added because a tamper widening the filter broke NOTHING in 51 tests.

steps.t: A real conflict still reports honestly
steps.evidence: NEGATIVE CONTROL: a genuine same-file divergence still returns ok=False and updated=False, so clearing blockers cannot turn a real conflict into a silent success.

steps.t: Verified on the owner's laptop
